# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 12 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 12 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_012_page_001.jpg

---

**12:1** Your imperishable Spirit permeates all things.

**12:2** And so, when people go wrong, you correct them gently, a little at a time. You confront them with their own sins as a reminder and a warning, so that they can turn away from evil and trust in you, Lord.

**12:3** Even the ancient inhabitants of your holy land — you hated them,

**12:4** because of the deeply detestable things they practiced: sorcery, impious rituals,

**12:5** the merciless killing of children, sacrificial feasts involving human flesh and blood conducted at the center of their initiation rites —

**12:6** parents who murdered their own helpless children. You planned to destroy them at the hands of our ancestors,

**12:7** so that the land you loved most could become home to people worthy to be called God's own children.

**12:8** And yet even these people you treated with the mercy one extends to fellow human beings. You sent hornets ahead of your armies to drive them out bit by bit.

**12:9** It wasn't that you lacked the ability to hand the ungodly over to the righteous in open battle, or to wipe them out instantly with terrifying animals or a single devastating word.

**12:10** But you judged them one step at a time, leaving room for repentance. You were not naive — you knew their origins were evil, their wickedness was baked in, and their mindset would never truly change.

**12:11** They were a cursed people from the very beginning. But your restraint did not come from any fear of consequences.

**12:12** Who could ever challenge you: "What do you think you're doing?" Who could oppose your verdict? Who could bring charges against you for wiping out nations you yourself created? Who would dare stand in your court as a defense attorney for the guilty?

**12:13** There is no other god alongside you who cares for everything, to whom you owe an explanation that your verdicts are just.

**12:14** No king, no ruler can face you down to protect those you have sentenced.

**12:15** You are righteous, and so you govern everything with justice. You consider it beneath your power to punish someone who does not deserve it.

**12:16** Your strength is precisely what makes you just; and because your authority extends over all things, you show forbearance toward all.

**12:17** You demonstrate your strength when doubters question whether your power is really unlimited — and you correct the arrogance of those who should know better.

**12:18** But you, with all that power at your disposal, judge with patient restraint and govern us with extraordinary gentleness — because the power is always there, ready, whenever you decide to use it.

**12:19** Through these actions you taught your people something: the righteous person must be a friend to humanity. And you gave your children wonderful reason for hope — that you are willing to grant forgiveness to those who sin.

**12:20** If this is how carefully and patiently you treated the enemies of your own people — people who truly deserved to die — giving them time and opportunity to break free from their wickedness,

**12:21** then how much more precisely and carefully did you hold your own children to account — the descendants of those with whom you swore solemn covenants and made glorious promises?

**12:22** So while you discipline us, you strike our enemies with blows a thousand times greater — so that when we sit in judgment we will remember your goodness, and when we are judged ourselves, we will be hoping for mercy.

**12:23** This is also why you tormented those who lived their lives in foolishness and wickedness — you used the very things they worshipped as the instruments of their punishment.

**12:24** They had gone hopelessly astray down wrong paths, treating as gods the most contemptible animals — creatures even other animals would look down on — deceived as completely as small, silly children.

**12:25** So you sent them a judgment that matched their foolishness — a kind of divine mockery appropriate for unreasoning children.

**12:26** But those who laughed off the gentle, mocking correction — they will face a judgment that is no laughing matter: a judgment worthy of God himself.

**12:27** In the end, the things they were angry about suffering through — the very objects they had called gods — became the means by which they were punished. And through that punishment they finally saw and acknowledged the true God, the one they had previously refused to recognize. And so the full weight of condemnation came down on them.
